history.period: Constructed 1993-1997; functioning since the late 1990s (verify inauguration date)
history.summary: NOT A TEMPLE OR CHURCH - Saikuti Hall is a community auditorium and cultural centre, described as the biggest hall in Mizoram. Built 1993-1997 as a PWD Government of Mizoram consultancy project (Archtech Consultants), it is an auditorium of about 1,200 seats with a 100-seat conference hall, a museum, a library and a restaurant, with roughly 65,000 sq.ft. built-up area. The hall is named after Saikuti, the celebrated Mizo poetess/composer of the traditional Saikuti zai folk songs (one travel source instead describes her as 'Saikuti Sailo' - the poetess attribution is flagged as needing confirmation). It sits in the heart of Lunglei city and is the town's principal venue: most concerts and celebrations in Lunglei are held here, along with church conferences, seminars, exhibitions and public gatherings. A museum established in the hall has local painters demonstrate their skill and exhibit their works; the library holds books on Mizo tradition and culture. Polling and election administration events also use it (polling parties for the 2024 Lok Sabha election were flagged off from Saikuti Hall). Entry is generally free except for ticketed events; one tourism guide lists weekday hours 9 AM-5 PM (Sat 9 AM-2 PM), closed Sundays and public holidays (verify).

town_description: Lunglei is the second-largest town of Mizoram and the headquarters of Lunglei district, about 165-200 km south of Aizawl. 'Lunglei' means 'bridge of rock', from a rock formation near Nghasih, a tributary of the Tlawng river. The town is noted for Saikuti Hall (its cultural hub), Thuamluaia Mual football stadium, Zobawk Sports Academy, Kawmzawl Park, and the nearby Khawnglung Wildlife Sanctuary. Connected to Aizawl by bus/jeep; a Pawan Hans helicopter service also operates between the two cities (verify current status).

travel.airport: Lengpui Airport (Aizawl, IATA: AJL) - the nearest commercial airport, about 170-200 km from Lunglei (verify); helicopter service between Aizawl and Lunglei has operated (verify current status). Plans for a small airport at Kawmzawl, ~25 km from Lunglei, have been reported (verify).
travel.railway: No railway station at Lunglei; the nearest railhead is on the Bairabi-Sairang line (verify current connectivity), with onward road travel to Lunglei.
travel.road: Lunglei is about 165-200 km south of Aizawl, connected by regular buses and shared sumos/jeeps (verify timings). Saikuti Hall is in the heart of Lunglei city, easily reached by taxi/auto within the town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Visit during a concert or cultural event to see the hall in use; check local posters, social media or the tourism office for the event calendar.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One tourism guide lists 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Monday-Friday and 9:00 AM-2:00 PM Saturday, closed Sundays and public holidays (verify - hours depend on scheduled events). Entry is generally free; ticketed events may charge.
